name: fix_asyncio_blocking_sleep
description: Replaces an event-loop-blocking time.sleep with asyncio.sleep
prompts: poll_sensor in sensors.py calls time.sleep inside a coroutine - which blocks the entire event loop, so 'concurrent' polls of 5 sensors take 500ms instead of 100ms and starve every other task on the loop. Fix sensors.py to await asyncio.sleep instead. The returned dict shape stays {'sensor': id, 'value': id * 1.5}.

setup_files.sensors.py:
import time


async def poll_sensor(sensor_id):
    """Simulated 100ms sensor read. BUG: time.sleep blocks the whole
    event loop - every other coroutine stalls while this one 'waits'."""
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return {'sensor': sensor_id, 'value': sensor_id * 1.5}

test_setup_files.test_sensors.py:
import asyncio
import time

from sensors import poll_sensor


async def main():
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    results = await asyncio.gather(*(poll_sensor(i) for i in range(1, 6)))
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0

    assert results[0] == {'sensor': 1, 'value': 1.5}, results[0]
    assert results[4] == {'sensor': 5, 'value': 7.5}, results[4]
    # blocking sleep serializes: ~0.5s. asyncio.sleep overlaps: ~0.1s.
    assert elapsed < 0.35, f'5 concurrent 100ms polls took {elapsed:.2f}s - the loop is being blocked'
    print(f'PASS ({elapsed:.2f}s)')


asyncio.run(main())

reference_solution.sensors.py:
import asyncio


async def poll_sensor(sensor_id):
    """Simulated 100ms sensor read."""
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    return {'sensor': sensor_id, 'value': sensor_id * 1.5}
